THE SURPRISE

Most of this already exists. It is pointed at software instead of at you.

• An agent is already a cross-space ROLE — a markdown file with role, system prompt, provider and permissions. Your "general role that works across spaces" IS an agent. They just happen to be architect, dev-a, qa, reviewer.

• A bot is already a per-space MANAGER — _bot.md with a goal and a rhythm. It wakes, keeps a plan, puts agents on work.

• The assistant can already CREATE bots from a sentence (BotDraft + BotMaker). It has simply never been the one to suggest it.

• Memory already splits general from scoped: a note with no project_id is general.

• And the personality is one line, seeded once to a file you own:
  "You are the developer's assistant. You coordinate the team, answer questions about the work, and keep track of what matters."

WHAT IS ACTUALLY MISSING

1. A persona that is not developer-shaped, and any way to choose or shape it.

2. A first run. There is none anywhere in the codebase — you land in an empty tree.

3. Life-shaped roles. Six agents, all software.

4. Bots with hands that are not code. The Fitness bot's goal is Koda and the gym; a bot's job is putting agents on work items in a repository. It wakes at 08:00 and can do nothing.

5. The assistant never proposes. It answers.

WHY MAIL IS THE RIGHT START — AND WHERE IT GOES WRONG

It is true: your mailbox knows your clients, your bills, who you actually talk to. And MailContact already carries name, role, company, thread count, last message and a node_id linking it to a client. This is a proposal layer over things that exist, not a new system.

Three ways it goes wrong, and the answers this screen commits to:

• A mailbox is mostly noise. Rank by reciprocity, not volume — Amazon sent 1,204 messages and you never replied once, so it is not a person.

• Reading a whole mailbox to build a profile is a big act. So nothing is kept until accepted, item by item, and a decline is remembered.

• Mailboxes hold passwords, one-time codes and card numbers. Those messages are skipped WHOLE — not summarised, not stored. Same rule the Stash already applies to your clipboard.

Say it plainly on screen, because this is the moment trust is either earned or lost.

THE LINE THAT KEEPS THIS SAFE

Your own rule, already in CLAUDE.md: anything about the USER goes in the personal store, which refuses to be created inside a git repository.

So:
  facts about YOU (how you work, your goals, your family) → personal memory, never in a commit
  facts about a THING (a client, an invoice, the dog's vet) → that node's deck, in the vault

Life content is still node state. That is the whole reason a Life space can exist without leaking you into a repo.

ON MONEY, LATER

You said email now, money later, and that ordering is right — money is the one where a mistake is not recoverable.

When it comes, it arrives as rows in the same permission table: a role gets money:read long before anything gets money:write, and "move money" should probably never exist as a grant at all — only "draft a payment for you to approve".

The matrix is what makes handing this thing your life safe. Every new reach is a row, and the default stays approval even when that is annoying.
